propositions: Four rendered non-bridge advanced parser factories (metrics, audit, bridge-fsck, bridge-probe) use bare argparse.HelpFormatter instead of version-pinned RebarHelpFormatter, creating width inconsistency (78 vs 80) and exposing them to py3.13 argparse divergences that silently stalify generated help artifacts

Help-backed routes' canonical artifacts are generated by gen_cli_help.py, which must pin formatter and width (80) across all help-backed routes to ensure byte-identical regeneration and prevent py3.13-specific rendering regressions

A contract test must enforce that all help-backed (rendered, not intercept, not hidden/retired) registered parser factories use a formatter subclassing RebarHelpFormatter, failing RED before the switch for the four affected factories

Switching the four factories to RebarHelpFormatter and regenerating artifacts drifts only wrapping help (width 78→80) in bridge-fsck.txt and its docs mirror; metrics/audit/bridge-probe have no wrapping help and remain byte-unchanged

Intercept-group advanced parsers (verify.py, reconcile, config, identity, enrich, certs, workflow, jira, llm families) are out of scope: gen_cli_help.py never renders them, and gen_cli_reference.py already canonicalizes their live --help cross-version via _unwrap_usage and _collapse_metavars
Cross-version byte-identity of generated artifacts must hold deterministically across py3.11, py3.12, and py3.13.15 to close the latent py3.13 staleness trap left by RP-05 S2d
